podcast.body: This cover of Jerry Jeff Walker's 1968 song was featured on their album "Uncle Charlie and His Dog Teddy." Producer Bill McEwan enhanced the studio recording by adding tape of an interview with his wife's great Uncle Charlie, whose dog, Teddy, howled in sync with Charlie's harmonica. The song reached number 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1970, remaining on the pop charts for 36 weeks, and was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2010. "I knew a man bowed jangles any dance for you."

podcast.body: This song was part of the repertoire performed by the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band during their historic 1977 tour of the Soviet Union. Although described as "not very rock and roll," the performance of such songs served the purpose of injecting American culture into the Soviet populace as part of a US soft power initiative. "Mr. Bold Jangoos. Mr. Bold Jangoos. Mr. Bold Jangoos. Dance. Yeah, okay, not very rock and roll, but they served the purpose."
